texts.preamble: Smt. Trishla Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2018 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-16114-2016 (Smt. Trishla Jain Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 15 Jabalpur, Dated : 20-02-2018
texts.facts: sh This petition under section 482 of the Code of Criminal e Procedure has been filed to invoke the extra-ordinary jurisdiction of ad this Court and to quash the criminal case being RCT No.7982/2010 Pr pending before Special Magistrate, Bhopal under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 [for short "Act of 1954"]. a hy 2. The prosecution story, in brief, is that the petitioner is a licencee of Rajshree Milk Centre. The respondent No.2 is the ad salesman of Milk Centre. The Food Inspector obtained the sample of M food item on 07.3.2009 from the shop- Rajshree Milk Centre at 168/105, New Market, District Bhopal. He suspected 'Mawa' (a milk of product) to be adulterated and after extending Form No.6, purchased rt sample of 750 gms. for Rs.100/- and obtained the receipt. He divided ou the same into 3 parts and sent one part to the State Laboratory for analysis. The remaining two parts were deposited with the office of C Deputy Director, Food & Drugs Administration, Local Health h Authority, Bhopal. The sample was found to be adulterated. By report ig dated 13.4.2009 food was found to be adulterated. On 02.5.2009, the H Food Inspector was directed to prosecute the accused persons. Therefore, criminal complaint was filed on 19.7.2010. 3. The petitioner appeared before the trial Court on 11.4.2011 and moved an application for analysis of the second sample on 27.4.2011. The application was allowed and the second sample of the Food Article was sent for analysis to the Central Food Laboratory on 18.7.2011. After the second sample, report has been received on 01.6.2016 stating that the sample could not be examined as it was putrefied and was not found fit for examination. The petitioner claims that her valuable right under section 13(2-A) of the Act of 1954 could not be availed, as the sample of the food was decomposed and, therefore, the Director, Food Central Laboratory cannot be requested to analyze the third sample, as the sample has been rendered unfit for analysis. 4. On behalf of the respondent/State, it is contended that after the sample was analyzed, report was received and it was found that the food is adulterated, therefore, proceeding was initiated. The Smt. Trishla Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46175084/ 1 petitioner did not appear before the trial Court in time. Hence, the delay was caused by the petitioner himself. Hence, the petitioner sh cannot take advantage of his absence. e 5. On perusal of the record it is apparent that first sample ad was collected by the Food Inspector on 07.3.2009. The food article Pr was found adulterated. It is stated that it is a milk product. The life of milk product would be only 10 months. Section 13(2) of the Act of a 1954 provides right to the accused for sending second sample, if the hy applicant decides to analyze the second part of the sample before the ad Central Food Laboratory. The second sample was sent for analysis on M 18.7.2011, which is after about 2 years and 4 months. The report of the Central Food Laboratory dated 01.6.2016 states that the same is unfit of for analysis. 6. In the case of State of Harayana vs. Unique Farmaid rt P.Ltd. and others, AIR 2000 SCW 1985 observed that the complaint ou was filed 19 months late and for this delay prosecution cannot thrust C blame on the petitioner. The sample sent for analysis after about 2 years 4 months is not fit for further examination. The second sample sent for Central Food Laboratory has been received with the report that it is not found fit for examination.
